newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania notes rated P-1 by Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania notes rated P-1 by Moody's.

text.p: Effective today, Moody's Investors Service has assigned a P-1 rating to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania's upcoming negotiated sale of General Obligation Bond Anticipation Notes, Series 1997A. The Commonwealth is offering general obligation bond anticipation notes to temporarily fund its capital outlays. The notes will be issued in the form of commercial paper in an amount not to exceed $60 million.

The commercial paper notes, like the bonds which will eventually fund the notes, are general obligations to which the state pledges its full faith and credit. Prime security for payment of these notes is provided by: the state's full faith and credit pledge backing these notes; Pennsylvania's demonstrated strong market access for its general obligation bonds, which are to be issued to retire the notes; and a revolving credit agreement with Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale which significantly strengthens note security by assuring timely access liquidity sufficient for payment of note principal.

The agreement sets few conditions under which the bank may refuse to advance funds, and the conditions are limited to events we consider unlikely in light of the state's above-average credit standing.
